items.title: Always stop: signs, red lights
items.simple: Always stop at a stop sign. Always stop at a red light. A flashing red light means stop too. Stop all the way. Go only when it is safe.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle at all stop signs, red traffic lights and flashing red signals.
items.mnemonic: Red means stop. Solid or flashing.

items.title: Leaving a driveway: stop first
items.simple: Coming out of a driveway, alley, building or parking lot? Stop before you cross the sidewalk or enter the street. Let all cars and people go first.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle when entering a street or crossing over a sidewalk from a driveway, alley, building or parking lot. When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must stop and yield to all traffic and pedestrians.
items.mnemonic: Driveway out? Stop and let everyone pass.

items.title: Railroad lights flashing: stop
items.simple: Lights are flashing at a railroad crossing? You must stop your vehicle. Always.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle at railroad crossings with flashing signals.
items.mnemonic: Lights flash at the tracks? Stop. Every time.

items.title: Flagger signals stop: stop
items.simple: Flaggers direct traffic in some places. When a flagger signals you to stop, you must stop.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle when signaled by flaggers directing traffic.

items.title: Police signal to stop: obey
items.simple: A police officer signals you to stop? You must stop. If you drive away, the officer may chase you. If the officer dies in that chase, it is a Class 4 felony.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle at the direction of a police officer. If you don't obey a law enforcement officer's signal to stop and the officer pursues you and is killed as a direct result of the pursuit, you will be guilty of a Class 4 felony.
items.mnemonic: Officer says stop? You stop.

items.title: In a crash? Stop there
items.simple: If you are in a crash, you must stop at the scene. Do not drive away.
items.official: You must always stop your vehicle at the scene of a crash in which you are involved.
items.mnemonic: In it? Stay at it.

items.title: Car ahead went? You still stop
items.simple: You are behind a car at a stop sign. That car stops and then goes. You still must stop at the sign yourself. Go when the way is clear.
items.official: When approaching a stop sign and the car in front of you proceeds, stop at the sign and proceed when the way is clear.
items.mnemonic: Every car stops. Every time.

items.title: School bus red lights: stop
items.simple: A stopped school bus has flashing red lights and its stop sign out. Stop, no matter which way you are coming from. Stay stopped until all people are clear and the bus moves.
items.official: You must stop for stopped school buses with flashing red lights and an extended stop sign when you approach from any direction on a highway, private road or school driveway. Stop and remain stopped until all persons are clear and the bus moves again.
items.mnemonic: Red lights, stop arm out: everyone stops.

items.title: Bus loading, no lights: stop
items.simple: A school bus is letting people on or off. Its lights are not on. You must still stop.
items.official: You must also stop if the bus is loading or unloading passengers and the signals are not on.
items.mnemonic: People getting on or off the bus? Stop, lights or not.

items.title: Bus across a median: no stop
items.simple: A median or barrier splits the road. The bus is on the other side. You are going the other way. You do not have to stop. Watch for people getting off the bus.
items.official: You do not have to stop if you are traveling in the opposite direction on a roadway with a median or barrier dividing the road and the bus is on the opposite side of the median or barrier. However, be prepared for unexpected actions by persons exiting the school bus.
items.mnemonic: Median between you? Go, but watch for kids.

items.title: Yield can also mean stop
items.simple: Yield means let others go first. Can't merge safely into traffic? Then you must stop. Wait for a safe gap.
items.official: Yield also means to stop if you cannot merge safely into the flow of traffic.
items.mnemonic: No gap? Yield becomes stop.

items.title: First to arrive goes first
items.simple: Cars come to an intersection from different directions at different times. The car that gets there first goes first.
items.official: When vehicles from different directions arrive at an intersection at different times, the vehicle that arrives first goes first.
items.mnemonic: First there, first through.

items.title: Same time: left yields to right
items.simple: Two cars reach an intersection at the same time. There are no signs or signals. The driver on the left lets the driver on the right go first.
items.official: When vehicles from different directions arrive at the same time at an intersection with no signs or signals, the driver on the left must allow the driver on the right to go first.
items.mnemonic: A tie? The right goes first.

items.title: Traffic lights out: all stop
items.simple: The traffic lights are not working. Every car must stop. Then the driver on the left lets the driver on the right go first.
items.official: If the traffic lights at an intersection are not working, all vehicles coming to the intersection must stop. The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
items.mnemonic: Lights out? Everyone stops. Then the right goes first.

items.title: Entrance ramp: yield to highway
items.simple: On a ramp getting onto an interstate? Cars already on the highway go first. You must yield to them.
items.official: Drivers entering an interstate from an entrance ramp must yield the right-of-way to traffic already on the highway.
items.mnemonic: On the ramp? Highway cars go first.

items.title: Yield to cars already in
items.simple: Cars already in an intersection or roundabout go first. If you are entering, you must yield to them.
items.official: Drivers entering any intersection or roundabout must yield to traffic already in it.
items.mnemonic: Already in? They go first.

items.title: Walkers and bikers crossing: yield
items.simple: People walking or biking across the street in a crosswalk go first. This includes intersections with no painted crosswalk. Stop and let them cross. Take extra care when turning on red.
items.official: You must always stop for pedestrians attempting to cross the street at a crosswalk. You must yield to pedestrians or bicyclists who are crossing a street within a clearly marked crosswalk or at an unmarked intersection. Remember that turns on red are especially hazardous to pedestrians.
items.mnemonic: Feet and pedals in the crosswalk go first.

items.title: Funeral processions: yield
items.simple: You must yield to a funeral procession. Do not cut through it, join it, or get in its way. Cars in the line may use hazard flashers.
items.official: You must yield to funeral processions. Do not cut through, join or interfere with a funeral procession. Unless led by a police escort, the lead vehicle in a funeral procession must obey all traffic signs and signals. Other drivers in the procession may follow carefully without stopping and may use hazard lights (flashers) to indicate they are in the procession.
items.mnemonic: Funeral line: don't cut in, don't join in.

items.title: Military convoys: yield
items.simple: You must yield to all military convoys. Never cut through a convoy. Never join one.
items.official: You must yield to all military convoys. Never cut through or join a military convoy.
items.mnemonic: Convoy: don't cut in, don't join in.

items.title: Stopped emergency or tow: move over
items.simple: An emergency vehicle or tow truck is stopped with flashing lights. Move to a lane not next to it if you safely can. If you cannot, slow down and pass with care.
items.official: Drivers must take specific actions when they see vehicles with flashing or blinking blue, red, amber (yellow) or white lights. When approaching a stationary emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights on a highway, proceed with caution and, if reasonable, change to a lane not next to the vehicle. If you are unable to safely change lanes, reduce your speed and proceed with caution. Violations can result in court suspension of your driver's license and demerit points on your driving record.
items.mnemonic: Lights on the shoulder? Move over or slow down.

items.title: Trash truck: 10 MPH, 2 feet
items.simple: Stopped trash truck ahead? 4 or more lanes: move to a lane not next to it. Fewer lanes, or can't move over? Slow to 10 MPH below the limit. Pass at least 2 feet to its left.
items.official: When passing stationary vehicles in the process of trash collection on a highway of at least four lanes, change to a lane not next to the vehicle, if you can change lanes safely. If on a highway of fewer than four lanes or if you are unable to change lanes, slow down to 10 miles per hour below the posted speed limit and pass at least two feet to the left of the vehicle.
items.mnemonic: Trash truck: 10 slower, 2 feet over.

items.title: Stopped mail truck: use caution
items.simple: A mail vehicle is stopped on the road. Pass it with caution. Keep a safe speed for the road.
items.official: When passing a stationary mail vehicle, proceed with caution and maintain a safe speed for highway conditions.

items.title: Hazard lights or flares: change lanes
items.simple: A stopped vehicle has hazard flashers on, caution signs out, or lit flares. You must change lanes and pass with caution.
items.official: When passing stationary vehicles that have activated vehicular hazard warning signal flashers, displayed caution signs, or been marked with properly lit flares or torches, you are required to make a lane change and proceed with caution.
items.mnemonic: Flashers, signs or flares? Change lanes.

items.title: Fire trucks at alarm: 500 feet
items.simple: Fire trucks are stopped to answer an alarm. You may not park within 500 feet of them.
items.official: You may not park within 500 feet of where fire trucks or equipment are stopped answering an alarm.
items.mnemonic: Fire alarm? Park 500 feet away. Same 500 as following an emergency vehicle.

items.title: Emergency vehicle ahead: 500 feet back
items.simple: An emergency vehicle ahead has its lights flashing. Never follow it closer than 500 feet.
items.official: Never follow an emergency vehicle closer than 500 feet when its lights are flashing.
items.mnemonic: Flashing lights ahead? Stay 500 feet back. Same 500 as fire alarm parking.

items.title: Siren behind you: pull over
items.simple: A police car, fire truck, rescue vehicle or ambulance comes up behind you. It has a siren or flashing lights. Pull over to the right edge right away. Stop until it passes.
items.official: When police, fire and rescue vehicles or ambulances approach you from behind your vehicle using a siren, flashing lights or both, you must immediately yield the right-of-way. Safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.
items.mnemonic: Siren behind? Right side, stop.

items.title: Oncoming emergency, no median: stop
items.simple: An emergency vehicle comes toward you in the other lane. The road has no median. Pull over to the edge of the road. Stop until it passes.
items.official: When emergency vehicles approach you in the opposite lane on an undivided highway, you must pull over to the edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle passes.
items.mnemonic: No median? Pull over for sirens coming or going.

items.title: Work zones: pull-over exception
items.simple: In a highway work zone, the pull-over rules do not apply. That goes for emergency vehicles behind you and emergency vehicles coming toward you.
items.official: The requirements for emergency vehicles approaching from the same or opposite direction do not apply in highway work zones.

items.title: Entering a roundabout: yield
items.simple: Every road into a roundabout has a yield sign. There may be a yield line too. Slow down. Let people walking, bikes, and cars already in the circle go first.
items.official: Entering traffic must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, and to traffic already in the circle. Each road approaching the roundabout is marked with a yield sign and may also have yield line markings on the pavement. When approaching a roundabout, slow down. When you arrive at the roundabout, yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and bicyclists.
items.mnemonic: Roundabout: slow, yield, then enter.

items.title: Roundabouts: drive counter-clockwise
items.simple: A roundabout is a circle-shaped intersection with an island in the middle. Once inside, you drive counter-clockwise. That is the opposite way a clock's hands move.
items.official: Roundabouts are circular intersections with an island in the center and have one or more lanes. After entering the roundabout, drivers must travel in a counter-clockwise direction.
items.mnemonic: In the circle, counter the clock.

items.title: Roundabout lanes: pick by exit
items.simple: Turning right? Stay to the right as you enter. Turning left? Stay to the left. Going straight in a two-lane roundabout? Either lane is OK. Use your turn signals.
items.official: Use your turn signals to indicate where you want to go. If you plan to turn right, stay to the right as you enter the roundabout. If you plan to go straight, you may stay in either lane (if it is a dual lane circular intersection). If you plan to turn left, stay to the left as you enter the roundabout.
items.mnemonic: Right turn, right lane. Left turn, left lane.

items.title: Leaving a roundabout: right signal
items.simple: Inside the roundabout, stay in your lane until you are ready to exit. Use your right turn signal to exit. Before you exit, glance over your shoulder for cars in your blind spot.
items.official: While inside the roundabout, stay in your lane until you are ready to exit. Use your vehicle's right turn signal to let drivers around you know what you want to do. Do not change lanes or take an exit before checking for vehicles that may be continuing through the roundabout in the lane next to you or behind you. Quickly glance over your shoulder and check for any vehicles that may be in your blind spot.
items.mnemonic: Exit right: right signal plus a shoulder check.

items.title: Roundabout: read signs to pick exit
items.simple: Coming up to a roundabout? Slow down. Look for street and direction signs before you get there. They help you know which exit to take.
items.official: As you approach the roundabout, slow down; look for the street and direction signs. This will help you know which exit to take. These signs should be posted along the roadside before you reach the roundabout.
items.mnemonic: Read the signs before the circle.

items.title: Roundabout entry: obey, enter when clear
items.simple: Some roundabout entries have a stop sign, a yield sign or a traffic light. Obey it. Enter only when the way is clear.
items.official: Sometimes your entry point will be controlled by a stop or yield sign, or traffic signal. When the way is clear, you may enter the roundabout.

questions.explain: You must stop if the bus is loading or unloading passengers, even when the signals are not on.

questions.prompt: You must stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading passengers:
choices: Only when its red lights are flashing
Only when its stop arm is out
Even if its signals are not on
questions.explain: You must also stop if the bus is loading or unloading and the signals are not on.

questions.prompt: A school bus with flashing red lights is stopped on the other side of a median. You are going the opposite way. You:
choices: Must stop until the bus moves
Do not have to stop, but watch for people leaving the bus
Must stop only if children are crossing
Must change to the left lane
questions.explain: With a median or barrier between you and the bus, you do not have to stop, but watch for people leaving the bus.

questions.prompt: When may you pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights without stopping?
choices: When no children are in sight
When you are behind the bus
On a two-lane road with no median
When a median or barrier divides you from the bus and you go the opposite way
questions.explain: You need not stop only when going the opposite way with a median or barrier between you and the bus.

questions.prompt: At this sign, if you cannot merge safely into traffic, you must:
questions.explain: Yield also means to stop if you cannot merge safely.

questions.prompt: Yield also means:
choices: Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
Stop if you cannot merge safely
Traffic must make room for you
questions.explain: Yield also means to stop if you cannot merge safely into the flow of traffic.

questions.prompt: When vehicles from different directions arrive at an intersection at different times:
choices: The vehicle on the right goes first
The vehicle that arrives first goes first
The vehicle turning left goes first
questions.explain: The vehicle that arrives first goes first.

questions.prompt: A car from another direction reached the intersection before you. Who goes first?
choices: The other car, because it arrived first
You, if you are going straight
You, if the other car is turning
questions.explain: At different arrival times, the first to arrive goes first.

questions.prompt: Two vehicles arrive at the same time at an intersection with no signs or signals. Which driver must yield?
choices: The driver in the larger vehicle
questions.explain: The driver on the left must allow the driver on the right to go first.

questions.prompt: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you and a car on your right arrive at the same time. You must:
choices: Go first because you are on the left
Go first if you are going straight
Let the driver on the right go first
questions.explain: When you arrive together, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

questions.prompt: When the traffic lights at an intersection are out like this, you must:
choices: Stop, and the driver on the left yields to the right
Go if you are on the main road
Stop only if cars are coming
questions.explain: If the lights are not working, all vehicles must stop and the driver on the left yields to the right.

questions.prompt: If the traffic lights are not working at an intersection:
choices: Main road traffic does not need to stop
Only vehicles turning left must stop
Drivers on the right must stop
questions.explain: All vehicles coming to the intersection must stop.

questions.prompt: The lights at this intersection are not working. You and a car on your left arrive at the same time. Who goes first?
questions.explain: The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.prompt: Drivers entering an interstate from an entrance ramp must:
choices: Expect highway traffic to let them in
Stop at the end of the ramp every time
Yield the right-of-way to traffic already on the highway
Use the shoulder to speed up
questions.explain: Drivers on an entrance ramp must yield to traffic already on the highway.

questions.prompt: When you enter an interstate from a ramp, who has the right-of-way?
questions.explain: Traffic already on the highway has the right-of-way.

questions.prompt: When you enter any intersection or roundabout, you must yield to:
choices: Only traffic coming from the right
questions.explain: Drivers entering any intersection or roundabout must yield to traffic already in it.

questions.prompt: A car is already inside the intersection when you arrive. Who has the right-of-way?
choices: You, if you are going straight
You, if you are on the right
The car already in the intersection
questions.explain: Traffic already in the intersection has the right-of-way.

questions.prompt: You must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the street:
choices: In a marked crosswalk or at an unmarked intersection
Only when they have a walk signal
questions.explain: Yield to pedestrians or bicyclists in a clearly marked crosswalk or at an unmarked intersection.

questions.prompt: Turns on red are especially hazardous to:
questions.explain: Remember that turns on red are especially hazardous to pedestrians.

questions.prompt: A pedestrian is trying to cross the street at a crosswalk ahead. You must:
questions.explain: You must always stop for pedestrians attempting to cross at a crosswalk.

questions.prompt: You see this sign and a person is crossing in the crosswalk. You must:
questions.explain: You must yield to pedestrians crossing in a crosswalk.

questions.prompt: When you meet a funeral procession, you must:
choices: Join the end of the line
Yield and not cut through or join it
questions.explain: You must yield to funeral processions and not cut through, join or interfere with them.

questions.prompt: Unless led by a police escort, the lead vehicle in a funeral procession must:
choices: Obey all traffic signs and signals
questions.explain: The lead vehicle must obey all traffic signs and signals unless a police escort leads.

questions.prompt: Other drivers in a funeral procession may:
choices: Pass other cars in the procession
Follow carefully without stopping and use hazard flashers
questions.explain: Drivers in the procession may follow carefully without stopping and may use hazard lights.

questions.prompt: When you meet a military convoy, you must:
choices: Yield and never cut through or join it
questions.explain: You must yield to all military convoys and never cut through or join one.

questions.prompt: You must always yield the right-of-way to:
questions.explain: You must yield to all military convoys.

questions.prompt: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle or tow truck with flashing lights on a highway, you should:
choices: Speed up to pass it quickly
Change to a lane not next to it if you safely can
Stop behind it until it leaves
questions.explain: If reasonable and safe, change to a lane not next to the stopped vehicle.

questions.prompt: If you cannot safely change lanes when passing a stopped tow truck with flashing lights, you must:
choices: Reduce your speed and proceed with caution
questions.explain: If you cannot change lanes safely, reduce your speed and proceed with caution.

questions.prompt: Not moving over or slowing for a stopped emergency vehicle can result in:
choices: Court suspension of your license and demerit points
No penalty if no one is hurt
questions.explain: Violations can result in court suspension of your license and demerit points.

questions.prompt: Drivers must take specific actions when they see vehicles with flashing lights that are:
questions.explain: The rules cover flashing blue, red, amber (yellow) or white lights.

questions.prompt: On a highway with fewer than four lanes, when passing a stopped trash collection vehicle you must:
choices: Keep your speed and pass at least 1 foot away
Slow to 10 MPH below the limit and pass at least 2 feet to its left
Slow to 5 MPH below the limit and pass at least 3 feet to its left
questions.explain: Slow to 10 MPH below the posted limit and pass at least two feet to the left.

questions.prompt: On a highway of at least four lanes, when passing a stopped trash truck you should:
choices: Change to a lane not next to it, if you can do so safely
questions.explain: On four or more lanes, change to a lane not next to the trash truck if safe.

questions.prompt: When you cannot change lanes, you must pass a stopped trash truck at least how far to its left?
questions.explain: Pass at least two feet to the left of the trash collection vehicle.

questions.prompt: When passing a stopped mail vehicle, you should:
choices: Speed up to get by quickly
Proceed with caution at a safe speed
questions.explain: Proceed with caution and keep a safe speed for highway conditions.

questions.prompt: A mail vehicle is stopped along the road ahead. The law says to:
choices: Proceed with caution and keep a safe speed
questions.explain: When passing a stopped mail vehicle, proceed with caution at a safe speed.

questions.prompt: When passing a stopped vehicle that has its hazard flashers on, caution signs out or lit flares, you must:
choices: Change lanes and proceed with caution
questions.explain: You are required to make a lane change and proceed with caution.

questions.prompt: Lit flares or torches behind a stopped vehicle mean you must:
choices: Make a lane change and proceed with caution
Turn on your own flashers and stop
questions.explain: Lit flares or torches behind a stopped vehicle mean you must change lanes and proceed with caution.

questions.prompt: You may not park within ___ feet of where fire trucks are stopped answering an alarm.
questions.explain: You may not park within 500 feet of fire trucks or equipment answering an alarm.

questions.prompt: Where fire trucks or equipment are stopped answering an alarm, you may not park within:
questions.explain: The no-parking distance near fire trucks answering an alarm is 500 feet.

questions.prompt: When an emergency vehicle has its lights flashing, you should never follow closer than:
questions.explain: Never follow an emergency vehicle closer than 500 feet when its lights are flashing.

questions.prompt: You are driving behind a fire truck with flashing lights. You should:
choices: Follow closely to get through traffic
Stay at least 500 feet behind it
questions.explain: Never follow an emergency vehicle closer than 500 feet when its lights are flashing.

questions.prompt: When an emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights approaches from behind, you must:
choices: Stop in your lane right away
Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes
Pull to the left and keep driving
questions.explain: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

questions.prompt: An ambulance with flashing lights but no siren is coming up behind you. You must yield:
choices: Only if it also uses a siren
questions.explain: A siren, flashing lights or both means you must immediately yield the right-of-way.

questions.prompt: When an emergency vehicle approaches from the opposite direction on an undivided highway, you must:
choices: Keep driving at the same speed
Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes
questions.explain: On an undivided highway, pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.prompt: You must pull over and stop for an emergency vehicle coming from the opposite direction when:
choices: You are in the left lane
questions.explain: The pull-over rule for oncoming emergency vehicles applies on an undivided highway.

questions.prompt: The requirements to pull over and stop for approaching emergency vehicles do not apply:
questions.explain: These requirements do not apply in highway work zones.

questions.prompt: In a highway work zone, the rules for pulling over for approaching emergency vehicles:
questions.explain: The emergency vehicle pull-over requirements do not apply in highway work zones.

questions.prompt: This sign warns of a roundabout ahead. When you enter the roundabout, you must yield to:
choices: No one; circle traffic yields to you
Pedestrians and traffic already in the circle
questions.explain: Entering traffic must yield to pedestrians and to traffic already in the circle.

questions.prompt: Each road approaching a roundabout is marked with a:
questions.explain: Each road approaching a roundabout has a yield sign and may also have a yield line.

questions.prompt: As you approach a roundabout, you should:
choices: Speed up to find a gap
questions.explain: When approaching a roundabout, slow down.

questions.prompt: After entering a roundabout, drivers must travel:
questions.explain: After entering a roundabout, drivers must travel counter-clockwise.

questions.prompt: A roundabout is:
choices: A circular intersection with an island in the center
questions.explain: Roundabouts are circular intersections with an island in the center and one or more lanes.

questions.prompt: If you plan to turn left at a two-lane roundabout, you should:
choices: Stay to the right as you enter
Stay to the left as you enter
questions.explain: If you plan to turn left, stay to the left as you enter the roundabout.

questions.prompt: If you plan to go straight through a dual-lane roundabout, you may:
questions.explain: To go straight in a dual-lane roundabout, you may stay in either lane.

questions.prompt: If you plan to turn right at a roundabout, you should:
choices: Stay to the left as you enter
Use the lane closest to the island
Go around the whole circle first
Stay to the right as you enter
questions.explain: If you plan to turn right, stay to the right as you enter the roundabout.

questions.prompt: When you are ready to exit a roundabout, you should:
questions.explain: Use your right turn signal to show you are exiting.

questions.prompt: While driving inside a roundabout, you should:
choices: Stay in your lane until you are ready to exit
Change lanes often to find your exit
questions.explain: Stay in your lane until you are ready to exit.

questions.prompt: Before you change lanes or take an exit in a roundabout, you should:
choices: Glance over your shoulder for vehicles in your blind spot
Look only in your rearview mirror
questions.explain: Quickly glance over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.prompt: As you approach a roundabout, street and direction signs help you:
choices: Know how fast other cars are going
questions.explain: Looking for street and direction signs helps you know which exit to take.

questions.prompt: Street and direction signs for a roundabout should be posted:
choices: On the pavement inside the circle
Along the roadside before you reach the roundabout
questions.explain: These signs should be posted along the roadside before you reach the roundabout.

questions.prompt: You may enter a roundabout when:
choices: A car in the circle honks at you
questions.explain: When the way is clear, you may enter the roundabout.

questions.prompt: The entry point to a roundabout may sometimes be controlled by:
choices: A stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal
questions.explain: Sometimes the entry point is controlled by a stop or yield sign, or a traffic signal.
